title: Hatch product foundation direction review
summary: Three intentionally distinct directions for a trustworthy, local-first Agent design-system toolkit.

comparisonScenario.title: Create the UI foundation
comparisonScenario.description: A fixed desktop card shows the same Icon, Input, status message and primary Button so reviewers compare visual language instead of different content.

candidates.name: Precision Grid
candidates.designRationale: A dark, rational workspace makes system boundaries, machine-readable status and deterministic actions feel explicit. A strict grid and restrained green signal color support a technical tool without imitating a terminal.
candidates.differentiation: The most technical and information-dense option, using squared geometry, tabular rhythm and one operational accent.

colorStrategy.rationale: Near-black slate establishes focus; white text preserves readability; green is reserved for verified or ready states and never carries meaning alone.

palette.rationale: Deep slate reduces glare while keeping the workspace neutral.
A visible but restrained elevation step for panels.
High-contrast primary copy on dark surfaces.
Secondary information remains readable without competing.
Operational green marks ready and successful actions.

typography.heading: Inter Variable 650
typography.rationale: One variable family keeps the system economical; tabular numerals and clear weights support identifiers and status.

radius.strategy: Small radii communicate precision while preserving enough softness for approachable controls.

density.rationale: Compact vertical rhythm favors professional workflows while maintaining 44-pixel interactive targets.

candidates.graphicLanguage: Twelve-column alignment, one-pixel dividers, quiet panels and small uppercase metadata labels. Decoration is replaced by meaningful state structure.
candidates.iconography: Two-pixel outline SVG icons on a 24-pixel grid, with rounded joins and text labels for critical actions.
candidates.motion: Subtle 150–200 millisecond opacity and 8-pixel translation for state changes, with reduced-motion support and no decorative loops.
accessibilityPlan: Target WCAG 2.2 AA contrast and verify accent-on-dark combinations before Token approval.
Pair every status color with an icon and visible text; preserve keyboard focus rings.
benefits: Makes deterministic system state and engineering precision immediately credible.
Supports dense desktop workflows without introducing many visual primitives.
risks: A dark technical tone may feel intimidating to designers who expect a visual studio.
Compact rhythm needs disciplined hierarchy to avoid appearing like a developer console.

preview.title: Precision Grid foundation card
preview.altText: Dark slate foundation card with a green status accent, compact input and squared primary action.

candidates.name: Warm Studio
candidates.designRationale: A light, editorial workspace frames Hatch as a collaboration surface shared by designers and agents. Warm neutrals, generous spacing and confident type reduce the emotional distance of governance tasks.
candidates.differentiation: The most human and design-led option, favoring editorial hierarchy, soft surfaces and calm conversational guidance.

colorStrategy.rationale: Warm paper tones create a studio feel; dark ink anchors information; terracotta highlights deliberate human actions rather than machine status.

palette.rationale: Warm neutral canvas avoids sterile pure white.
Near-white cards preserve separation without heavy shadows.
Soft black keeps long-form guidance comfortable and clear.
Warm gray maintains hierarchy for supporting information.
Terracotta gives human approvals and primary actions distinction.

typography.heading: Manrope Variable 650
typography.rationale: Expressive rounded headings signal approachability while a neutral body face protects interface clarity.

radius.strategy: Moderate radii create tactility without turning professional controls into playful capsules.

density.rationale: Generous grouping helps mixed technical and design audiences understand one decision at a time.

candidates.graphicLanguage: Editorial blocks, warm hairline borders, modest paper-like depth and short explanatory annotations around important decisions.
candidates.iconography: Rounded outline SVG icons with slightly wider optical proportions, always paired with direct labels in approval flows.
candidates.motion: Calm 180–240 millisecond fades and scale shifts for panels; motion reinforces conversational progress and honors reduced-motion preferences.
accessibilityPlan: Verify terracotta text and controls against both warm backgrounds at WCAG 2.2 AA thresholds.
Keep body text at 16 pixels or larger with 1.5 line height and a persistent keyboard focus treatment.
benefits: Feels welcoming to professional designers while keeping governance understandable.
Creates room for rationale and review notes without resembling infrastructure software.
risks: Relaxed spacing may reduce efficiency in future component inventories and audit views.
The editorial tone could understate technical precision if status details are not carefully structured.

preview.title: Warm Studio foundation card
preview.altText: Warm cream foundation card with terracotta action, generous spacing and editorial typography.

candidates.name: Signal Layer
candidates.designRationale: A bright modular direction treats every design-system decision as a visible layer. Strong blue and citrus accents, bold labels and structured cards make Agent activity legible while preserving a serious core.
candidates.differentiation: The most distinctive and product-forward option, using modular composition, high contrast and visible state layers to create a recognizable identity.

colorStrategy.rationale: A cool white canvas protects clarity; navy carries text; electric blue owns primary actions; citrus is limited to attention and progress indicators.

palette.rationale: Cool near-white supports clean modular grouping.
Pure white makes cards crisp against the cool canvas.
Deep navy creates strong readable hierarchy.
Accessible blue defines links and primary controls.
Citrus highlights progress only when accompanied by dark text and shape.

typography.heading: Space Grotesk Variable 650
typography.rationale: A geometric display face adds product character; neutral body typography keeps contracts and status text stable.

radius.strategy: A stepped radius system distinguishes small controls from larger workflow surfaces.

density.rationale: Balanced spacing supports both onboarding explanations and operational catalogs without switching visual systems.

candidates.graphicLanguage: Stacked modules, offset status tags, strong border contrast and occasional signal blocks that reveal the boundary between Agent proposal and human approval.
candidates.iconography: Geometric two-pixel SVG icons with a consistent 24-pixel box; filled signal badges are reserved for workflow status.
candidates.motion: Purposeful 160–220 millisecond layer transitions show state replacement and provenance; all movement degrades to opacity under reduced motion.
accessibilityPlan: Use citrus only with dark foreground and never as the sole carrier of pending or warning status.
Test modular reading order, focus order and 44-pixel action targets at desktop and narrow widths.
benefits: Builds a recognizable identity suited to demos, documentation and future product surfaces.
Makes Agent-versus-human workflow boundaries visually memorable and easy to explain.
risks: Strong accents can become noisy if every module competes for attention.
The display typography and signal color require tighter governance than the neutral alternatives.

preview.title: Signal Layer foundation card
preview.altText: Cool white modular card with strong blue controls and a citrus workflow status layer.
